quick: 2.5 mg PO three times daily; titrate up to ~30 mg/day
With or after food to reduce GI upset
Use only if clearly needed; limited data
Caution; may suppress lactation and pass into milk
summary: Procyclidine is a centrally acting antimuscarinic used mainly for drug-induced extrapyramidal symptoms (parkinsonism, dystonia, akathisia) and as adjunct therapy in idiopathic Parkinson disease, where it helps tremor and rigidity more than bradykinesia. An injectable form rapidly relieves acute dystonic reactions. Typical anticholinergic adverse effects and contraindications (glaucoma, urinary/GI obstruction) apply, and it should be withdrawn gradually.
indications: Drug-induced extrapyramidal symptoms (parkinsonism, acute dystonia, akathisia) from antipsychotics and other agents
Symptomatic treatment of idiopathic, post-encephalitic and arteriosclerotic Parkinson disease (adjunct, especially for tremor and rigidity)
Acute dystonic reactions / oculogyric crises (parenteral procyclidine for rapid relief)

dosage.n: Increase gradually by 2.5 mg/day as needed

dosage.d: Usual 10-30 mg/day in divided doses (occasionally up to 60 mg/day)
5-10 mg IM or IV; repeat if needed (usually relieved within 5-10 min IV)
Start at the lower end and titrate slowly

admin: Take oral doses with or after food to reduce gastrointestinal upset (or before meals if dry mouth is troublesome)
Titrate slowly to balance benefit against anticholinergic adverse effects
For acute dystonia give IM or IV; IV relief is usually rapid
Do not stop abruptly - withdraw gradually to avoid rebound symptoms
Use the lowest effective dose, especially in the elderly
moa: Procyclidine is a competitive antagonist at central muscarinic acetylcholine receptors. In parkinsonism and drug-induced extrapyramidal syndromes, dopamine deficiency (or dopamine-receptor blockade) leaves relative cholinergic overactivity in the striatum. By blocking these muscarinic receptors, procyclidine restores the dopamine-acetylcholine balance, reducing tremor, rigidity and dystonia. It also has a mild antispasmodic effect on smooth muscle.
preg: There are limited data. Use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk; anticholinergics may cause neonatal effects if used near term.
lact: Caution: anticholinergics can suppress lactation and may pass into breast milk. Weigh benefit against risk; monitor the infant.
renal: Limited data; use with caution and at lower doses in significant renal impairment.
hepatic: Limited data; use with caution in hepatic impairment.

major: Other anticholinergic agents (tricyclic antidepressants, antihistamines, antipsychotics, antispasmodics) - additive antimuscarinic toxicity (confusion, ileus, retention, hyperthermia)
moderate: Drugs reducing GI motility (opioids) - increased risk of paralytic ileus
Antipsychotics - may mask early signs of tardive dyskinesia and reduce some antipsychotic GI absorption
Levodopa - may reduce levodopa absorption (delayed gastric emptying); metoclopramide/domperidone GI effects antagonized
interactions.food: May be taken with or after food to reduce GI upset; no major food interaction.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; additive sedation and CNS effects.

serious: Confusion, hallucinations or psychosis (especially elderly or high dose)
emergency: Central anticholinergic syndrome (agitation, hyperthermia, delirium, coma)

monitoring: Anticholinergic adverse effects (dry mouth, vision, constipation, urinary symptoms)
Mental status and cognition, particularly in the elderly
Intraocular pressure in patients at risk of glaucoma
counsel: Take with or after food; do not stop suddenly - withdraw gradually
Expect dry mouth and possible blurred vision; sugar-free gum and fluids can help
Avoid driving until you know how it affects you and avoid alcohol
Be cautious in hot weather/exercise (reduced sweating, risk of overheating)
Report eye pain, difficulty passing urine, severe constipation or confusion
pk: Oral within ~30-45 min; IV relief of dystonia within 5-10 min
Several hours; supports two to three times daily dosing
Store at room temperature; protect from light
pearls: Not FDA-approved; procyclidine is approved/used via SmPC/BNF (UK and other countries) - dosing follows the SmPC/BNF
First-line for acute drug-induced dystonia: parenteral procyclidine gives rapid relief of dystonic reactions and oculogyric crises
Helps tremor and rigidity more than bradykinesia in Parkinson disease; usually adjunctive
Avoid in narrow-angle glaucoma, GI obstruction and urinary retention; use cautiously in the elderly (confusion)
Has misuse potential because of euphoriant anticholinergic effects; withdraw gradually to avoid rebound
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it and resume the usual schedule. Do not take a double dose.
overdose: Overdose produces a central anticholinergic syndrome: agitation, hallucinations, dilated pupils, dry flushed skin, hyperthermia, tachycardia, urinary retention and, in severe cases, seizures, coma and circulatory collapse. Treat with supportive care, control of hyperthermia and agitation (benzodiazepines), and consider physostigmine for severe central toxicity under monitoring. Activated charcoal if recent ingestion.
